question:
In a classroom investigation of matrix algebra, students work with three matrices of the same order: $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-3&4\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}5&-1\\2&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $C=\begin{bmatrix}-2&3\\1&6\end{bmatrix}$. Since all three matrices are of order $2\times2$, their sums are defined. The students are asked to compare results obtained by changing the order and grouping of matrix addition. They also investigate how multiplying matrices by scalars interacts with matrix addition. The calculations are intended to verify important properties rather than merely compute isolated matrix values.

(a) Calculate $A+B$ and $B+A$, and compare the results.

(b) Calculate $(A+B)+C$ and $A+(B+C)$, and verify the relevant property of matrix addition.

(c) Calculate $2(A+B)$ and $2A+2B$, and compare the results.

(d) Calculate $(2+3)A$ and $2A+3A$, and state the property verified.
explanation:
(a)
Adding corresponding entries, $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}1+5&2-1\\-3+2&4+0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$. Similarly, $B+A=\begin{bmatrix}5+1&-1+2\\2-3&0+4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$. Thus, $A+B=B+A$, verifying the commutative property of matrix addition.

(b)
From part (a), $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$. Therefore, $(A+B)+C=\begin{bmatrix}6-2&1+3\\-1+1&4+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\0&10\end{bmatrix}$. Also, $B+C=\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\3&6\end{bmatrix}$, so $A+(B+C)=\begin{bmatrix}1+3&2+2\\-3+3&4+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\0&10\end{bmatrix}$. Hence, $(A+B)+C=A+(B+C)$, verifying the associative property of matrix addition.

(c)
We have $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$. Therefore, $2(A+B)=\begin{bmatrix}12&2\\-2&8\end{bmatrix}$. Also, $2A=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-6&8\end{bmatrix}$ and $2B=\begin{bmatrix}10&-2\\4&0\end{bmatrix}$. Hence, $2A+2B=\begin{bmatrix}12&2\\-2&8\end{bmatrix}$. Thus, $2(A+B)=2A+2B$, verifying distributivity of scalar multiplication over matrix addition.

(d)
Since $2+3=5$, $(2+3)A=5A=\begin{bmatrix}5&10\\-15&20\end{bmatrix}$. Also, $2A+3A=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-6&8\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3&6\\-9&12\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5&10\\-15&20\end{bmatrix}$. Hence, $(2+3)A=2A+3A$, verifying the distributive property of scalar addition over a matrix.

options.A:
(a) $A+B=B+A=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$, verifying commutativity.
(b) Both groupings give $\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\0&10\end{bmatrix}$, verifying associativity.
(c) Both expressions give $\begin{bmatrix}12&2\\-2&8\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Both expressions give $\begin{bmatrix}5&10\\-15&20\end{bmatrix}$, verifying associativity of scalar multiplication.
options.C:
(a) $A+B=B+A=\begin{bmatrix}6&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$, verifying the commutative property of matrix addition.
(b) $(A+B)+C=A+(B+C)=\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\0&10\end{bmatrix}$, verifying associativity.
(c) $2(A+B)=2A+2B=\begin{bmatrix}12&2\\-2&8\end{bmatrix}$, verifying distributivity over matrix addition.
(d) $(2+3)A=2A+3A=\begin{bmatrix}5&10\\-15&20\end{bmatrix}$, verifying distributivity of scalar addition over a matrix.
options.D:
(a) $A+B=B+A=\begin{bmatrix}6&-1\\1&4\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Both groupings give $\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\0&10\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Both expressions give $\begin{bmatrix}12&2\\-2&8\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Both expressions give $\begin{bmatrix}5&10\\-15&20\end{bmatrix}$.
